title: So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE)
summary: First live physique review stream: NH critiques about 20 viewer physiques submitted via Ko-fi, covering strong and weak points, body fat, genetic gifts, bulk/cut decisions and program fixes, and grades each lifter from novice to advanced. He also tells how a retired strongman neighbour gave him about $1000 of strongman equipment. Recurring themes: lagging forearms, chest and hamstrings, leg-skipping, bulking too fast, overcomplicated novice programs, and how much a physique can change in 5 years.
claims: With average genetics it took him about 6 years from starting at 15 to look like he lifted, and more than 10 years to look actually jacked

A retired 45-year-old strongman neighbour gave him a Rogue yoke, a Husafell stone, a circus dumbbell, a Rogue sled and two 25 lb plates (about $1000) and delivered them; the man is now switching to bodybuilding
On rest days he lifts the strongman implements outdoors as light conditioning, and uses the 25 lb plates for finger curls
He never tells gym bros he meets that he makes videos because it changes the relationship; he wants to be seen as just a gym bro who has more training time than his viewers
Most submitted physiques came from novices, so the stream shows what an average physique really looks like; his own standards are skewed high
His review method: identify strong and weak points, estimate body fat to decide cut, recomp or bulk, spot undeveloped parts with great potential, then fix the program toward the stated goal
People paying for a review should send many photos and videos from several angles; one picture gives him nothing to work with
To load the abs when hanging leg raises get too heavy with a dumbbell, switch to knee raises
A bulk taken too far just makes you look like a fat guy with no definition; Agri (22, 5'10) lost only about 10 kg on a cut and suddenly showed back separation, arm definition and abs
Big love handles are not a death sentence: the waist is where the body stores fat and that fat does come off when you cut
For aesthetics you want a waistline close to your leg size; small legs with a small waist still keep the illusion
Someone who has escaped skinny-fat and is lean but small should do a lean, non-aggressive bulk
A chest program with only incline and decline dumbbell pressing and no flat movement is worth fixing; find a flat press you connect with
Even someone who says he deliberately deprioritizes back should still do plenty of back exercises at a small size

Austin, a former 7-year distance runner, reached a 465 lb squat, 315 bench and 505 deadlift powerlifting, but looked worse at 210 lb; recomping down to 175 lb at 5'9 gave a good, clean natural physique at about 10-12% body fat
A balanced or dominant quad teardrop is usually seen in jumpers and runners, not powerlifters; your athletic past stays with you in bodybuilding and is never wasted
To build the teardrop (VMO), do split squats as a priority
To build the mid back and rear delts for a front-dominant lifter, add rows done with the elbows flared

CalmThug (21, ~194 lb, 3 years of lifting while also doing Muay Thai and BJJ) deadlifts 600 lb, squats 545, does RDLs 4x8 at 455 and leg presses 600 for 20: freak genetics exist and no one could guess them from a photo
A separated upper-trap shelf is usually a genetic gift for the back
Deep, low tricep insertions look underwhelming early but give great potential for monster triceps with years of work, as with GVS
Some people store fat mostly in the front of the abdomen and will need direct ab training plus a cut to see a six-pack; he stores his in the back instead
Once you can do 25 clean bodyweight dips it is time to add weight; if the lower chest still lags with dips, try flat bench
Barbell curls with a straight bar may not be the best way to target the biceps, though a beginner can make them work
If you have a long abdomen relative to the torso you must train abs directly
Mirror shots in window light flatter the physique; under neutral lighting the real body fat and lagging delts show
A lifter with big arms and traps but no lats or mid back has a lobster physique, the opposite of the usual imbalance; he needs back work
Fat Jack looked like there was no hope, but after cutting 20-30 lb he revealed a great structure for bodybuilding: just lose the fat
A young lifter with good structure does not need steroids to reach a Toji-style physique; time and consistency are what he needs
He rates his own physique 6.5/10, Alex and GVS around 7-7.5, Bomman 6.5, Elak 8.5, and says he has never met a 10
Jeff, 5'11 and 210 lb at about 16-18% body fat, lacks tricep long head; weighted dips mostly go to an already dominant chest, so add an isolation that targets the long head
Not wanting overpowering legs is fine, but legs so small they detract from the physique have no merit; long legs are not an excuse
If hamstrings lag despite leg curls and RDLs, the cause may be genetics, too little volume, or RDLs that hit glutes more; push the bar further forward on RDLs
Never do 3x5 on isolations like dips or preacher curls, or on Bulgarian split squats; use higher, hypertrophy-focused rep ranges, keeping 3x5 for compounds like weighted chins
A physique built on 5 training days a week can be maintained on 2 days a week; naturals never really lose what they built unless they let go
Joey went from skinny-fat looking to shredded and balanced in 5 years (2 years messing around, 3 serious), proof that you don't need steroids
Five years of hard training makes most adults and teens look like a completely different person
For an advanced lean lifter wanting a new goal: focus on the yoke (traps), forearms and posterior chain, which work well together
Staying a perma-bulker is the way to go unless you start out fat
Steve Reeves said your calves should match your upper arms; if you want his physique, get 16 in calves for 16 in arms
Being in a bulk is no excuse for no six-pack: train your core directly
You can put dominant body parts like shoulders and traps on the back burner and specialize lagging ones (abs, lats, chest) in the program
Most bodybuilders, him included, have an overdeveloped outer quad and an underdeveloped VMO; split squats balance it
A thick neck can make you look like a thumb or like a total beast depending on the rest of the build
A non-shredded physique with a full delt sweep is maintainable year round; natural delts look swept rather than puffy like PED users' delts
Short arms tend to be a bodybuilding gift because the arms look bigger
A caloric surplus is your best weapon for progress in the gym, but a surplus is not the same as getting fat
A small, long-limbed former fat lifter should do a very slow, conservative bulk for the next five years, counting calories, and drop the overcomplicated program
Relaxed poses are important in reviews because you cannot hide weaknesses in them
A stomach vacuum only helps when there is enough mass on top; on a small frame it just looks starved
Waist size is structural; fat on it goes when you cut
With a long torso, the core becomes the focal point in poses, so prioritize core training
Beginners should start on an established program, not make their own, because they lack the data to program for themselves
Gaining 50 lb in 3 years is too fast unless you were dangerously skinny; at least ~20 lb of it was avoidable fat, now forcing a slow recomp or a performance-sapping cut
You don't need to gain tremendous amounts of fat to progress in hypertrophy
A tall, lean, thin lifter tired from night shifts should bulk: the extra calories give energy, and he can train less often but more intensely
StrongLifts 5x5 is a garbage program for hypertrophy; 2.5 years of it plus program hopping still leaves you a novice
There is no such thing as a non-responder to an absent stimulus; a skinny-fat novice just needs to train hard and gain muscle, and cut, bulk or recomp hardly matters
After a productive bulk that left lots of waist fat, either cut then bulk again, or recomp if happy; for aggressive cuts he points to GVS and Alex Leonidas
A novice should pick 4-5 movements per day, take them to failure and progressively overload; only add complexity later when needed to keep gaining
YouTubers overcomplicating training lead novices to run 40-exercise programs they don't need
At the same body fat, more lean mass makes you look leaner; the point of bulking is to gain the muscle that makes the fat look better
A high-fat, low-muscle novice should cut (e.g. to 80 kg) and can still build muscle on the cut
The novice phase is done within a year for many, but program hopping, bad programs or weak commitment can keep people novices for 3-4 years
A lifter who went from 130 kg to 64 kg with almost no loose skin then bulked to 77 kg; big calves are a leftover from being fat, and his quads now overpower his upper body, so ease off squats
Muscle does not turn into fat; when athletes quit and keep eating the same, the caloric surplus turns into fat
Losing a lot of weight without lifting leaves you skinny-fat; lifting while in the deficit keeps muscle underneath
Sammy's physique (fat to skinny-fat to jacked, 3 serious years) would be top 10 percent in most commercial gyms
Scott, 55, trained from 14 to 27, took 21 years off and restarted at about 50; he looks great for his age, proof that lifting preserves your looks
Scott built his gym in Thailand from bamboo and homemade concrete plates
Bad calf insertions are no excuse: Scott has poor insertions and still has good calves
Someone who has lifted 10 years for aesthetics shouldn't look like an early intermediate at best; BJJ and calisthenics training is not the same as training for aesthetics
Tat Ketun (23, Finland) beat cancer at 10 and benches 150 kg, squats 200 kg x4 and overhead presses 90 kg while looking shredded and aesthetic
Most powerlifters think they will look aesthetic from powerlifting, but almost none do
His ranking of the reviewed lifters ran from novice (most) through intermediate to advanced (Joey, Lenus); his favourite physique was Lenus for the mix of mass and leanness
exercises: use instead of leg raises when weighting with a dumbbell
progression; but chest-dominant lifters get mostly chest
maybe not best to target biceps
only useful with enough upper-body mass
viewer_questions: how many years of training to stop looking like you don't lift
is there selection bias in who sends physiques
should I cut or keep bulking
